label: D2 after choosing a1 and landing in S2 (a1 rare transition)
explanation: Fires only at D2, and only when the D2 inputs show last action a1 together with state S2, i.e. a rare transition after choosing a1. Recall is about 99.9% and it carries essentially all activation mass. It never fires at D1 or GO, on a1->S1, on a2->S2, or on a2->S1 (rare after a2), apart from 42 tiny activations. The roughly 27% false positives are a1->S2 steps where it stays silent: mostly early in the episode (requiring ep_trial >= 10 raises F1 from 0.84 to 0.86 and removes only low-quartile activations) and steps where the model value is high (requiring value < 7.6 gives precision 0.87, recall 0.85). Those refinements were not recorded because the gain is small. Every variable is observed at D2 (current inputs).

issues: The core claims hold on the test split. The unit never fires at D1 or GO (phase != D2: 0 active). It almost never fires at D2 outside a1->S2 (complement predicate recall 0.0013, mass 0.0005; 43 small misses). The recorded scores reproduce: P 0.707, R 0.999, F1 0.828, mass recall 0.999. It uses no future variables at D2.

Missed systematic class: when the agent switches into a1 (prev_action == 2) and lands in S2, the unit is mostly silent. Precision on that subset is 0.27 (897 of 3337 predicted steps active), against 0.74 when it repeats a1 (prev_action == 1). The explanation calls the false positives 'mostly early in the episode or high value' and never mentions this class. Excluding switch trials raises test F1 from 0.828 to 0.841.

Second systematic class: when the hidden good state is S2, precision on a1->S2 drops to 0.54 (vs 0.74 when S1 is good). That is a rare transition into the good state. It is likely what the 'value high' false positives reflect, so silence is tied to whether S2 is currently good, not just noise.
The ep_trial claim is weak. ep_trial >= 3 gives the same F1 gain as ep_trial >= 10 (0.843), and most of the early-trial effect is the first-window-trial boundary, not episode position.

Taken together, the 'rare after a1' label is correct as a necessary condition. But it overstates sufficiency: about 29% of a1->S2 D2 steps are silent, and they cluster in switch-into-a1 trials and S2-good contexts. These are not scattered noise.
skeptic.revised_label: D2 after a rare a1->S2 transition, mainly when a1 was a repeated choice and S2 is not the expected good state (low value). Silent on switch-into-a1 trials.
